The plates do not drift on their own. Heat escaping from deep inside the Earth keeps the mantle moving, and the plates ride on top of that motion.

```atlas-visual
alt: A callout: the mantle is solid rock that flows very slowly
{"root": "note", "elements": {"note": {"type": "callout", "props": {"title": "The mantle is not liquid", "body": "Mantle rock is solid, yet over millions of years it flows like very stiff putty."}, "children": []}}}
```

Hot rock rises beneath the ridges and cooler rock sinks at the trenches. Where the cold edge of a plate sinks, its weight drags the rest of the plate behind it.

